title: Financial Fortress: Budget Defense
description: Defend your financial future against waves of expenses! Build savings accounts, insurance policies, investments, and budget plans to stop monthly bills, impulse buys, debt, and emergency expenses from draining your resources. Learn real financial planning through strategic tower defense.
learning_objectives: Understand the importance of emergency funds and savings in financial planning
Learn how insurance protects against unexpected financial shocks
Practice budgeting by allocating limited resources across defense strategies
Recognize different types of expenses and their financial impact
Develop long-term investment thinking to build financial resilience
Experience the consequences of impulse spending and unmanaged debt
how_to_play: Waves of expenses (bills, impulse buys, debt, emergencies) march along the path toward your bank account.
Place financial defense towers adjacent to the path to stop them: Emergency Funds, Insurance Policies, Investments, and Budget Plans.
Each tower costs Savings to build — spend wisely! You earn more Savings for each expense you eliminate.
Upgrade your towers to increase their effectiveness against tougher expenses.
If too many expenses reach the end of the path, your finances are ruined — game over!
Survive all 8 waves to achieve financial stability and win!

storybook_pages.title: Your Financial Journey Begins
storybook_pages.text: You've just started managing your own finances. Bills are piling up, impulse purchases tempt you at every turn, and the specter of debt looms large. But you have tools: savings, insurance, investments, and a solid budget plan. Deploy them wisely to protect your financial future.
storybook_pages.image_prompt: young person at a desk surrounded by bills and receipts, a piggy bank and calculator nearby, a path leading to a bank vault with expense monsters approaching, cartoon financial education style

storybook_pages.title: Build Your Defenses
storybook_pages.text: An Emergency Fund is your first line of defense — reliable and always there when you need it. Insurance protects against groups of unexpected costs. Investments deal heavy damage but take time to pay off. Budget Plans slow down expenses so other defenses can handle them.
storybook_pages.image_prompt: four tower types illustrated as financial tools: a bank building (savings), a shield (insurance), a growing chart (investment), a clipboard (budget), positioned along a winding path, colorful cartoon style

storybook_pages.title: Financial Freedom
storybook_pages.text: Each wave of expenses you survive makes you financially stronger. The key is balance: don't overspend on one type of defense while neglecting others. By the end, you'll understand how real financial planning works — and you'll have the skills to protect your wallet in real life!
storybook_pages.image_prompt: triumphant scene of all expense waves defeated, towers standing strong, savings growing, a graduation cap on a piggy bank, confetti and financial freedom banner, celebratory cartoon style

rounds.coaching_moment: Think carefully about the trade-offs before committing to this path.
rounds.reflection_prompt: Why did you make this choice?

transfer_exercises.game_context: Prioritizing which threats to defend against first
transfer_exercises.real_world: Triaging tasks and problems by impact and urgency
transfer_exercises.challenge: Use the Eisenhower matrix to categorize your current tasks. Are you spending time on what actually matters?

transfer_exercises.real_world: Keeping quality high when workload unexpectedly doubles
transfer_exercises.challenge: Design a personal 'defense system' — habits and routines that protect your performance under stress.

glossary_terms.definition: The process of selecting among alternatives based on available information and values.
glossary_terms.example: Choosing between two career paths based on income, passion, and long-term growth.
glossary_terms.deep_dive: Good decision-making combines rational analysis with awareness of cognitive biases that distort judgment.
glossary_terms.real_world_example: Leaders make high-stakes decisions daily — the quality of their process matters as much as the decision itself.

glossary_terms.definition: Analyzing information objectively to form a well-reasoned judgment.
glossary_terms.example: Questioning whether a statistic is representative before using it to make a decision.
glossary_terms.deep_dive: Critical thinking involves identifying assumptions, evaluating evidence, and considering alternative perspectives.
glossary_terms.real_world_example: Journalists fact-check before publishing; scientists replicate experiments before claiming discoveries.

glossary_terms.definition: The belief that abilities can be developed through effort and learning from failure.
glossary_terms.example: Seeing a poor game result as feedback on what to practice, not evidence of being bad at the game.
glossary_terms.deep_dive: Research by Carol Dweck shows people with growth mindsets achieve more and recover better from setbacks.
glossary_terms.real_world_example: Students who believe intelligence is fixed give up when challenged; those with growth mindset persist and improve.

cultural_context: Financial fraud and digital payment security are major concerns as India's UPI-based economy grows to over 10 billion monthly transactions. This game builds the defensive financial thinking needed by India's digital-first generation.
reflection_prompt: Where did your defenses bend before they broke? What would you reinforce first next time?
